sentences.text: The facts of the present case are that the victim lodged a written report on 03.02.2022 to the effect that the petitioner who was appointed as Branch Manager of Adim Jati Sewa Sahakari Society Maryadit Shakha, Govindpur, sexually assaulted her in the month of October 2021, but she did not mention the date and time of the incident.

entities.text: Adim Jati Sewa Sahakari Society Maryadit Shakha
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is further stated that earlier her husband was working in society and therefore, the petitioner used to visit her house frequently.
On the date of the incident at about 11-12 P.M., the petitioner forcibly entered her house and sexually assaulted her.
It is also stated that she belongs to the Gond caste which falls under Scheduled Tribe.
It is further stated that when her husband came back, the matter was informed.
On such complaint, police registered the FIR on 03.02.2022 at about 16:40 hours for the commission of an offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC.

The police seized the caste certificate of the victim, she was medically examined on 05.02.2022 where the medical officer opined that there was no sign of recent sexual assault and no struggle marks were present.
Thereafter, a site plan was prepared and the statement under Sections 161 and 164 of the Cr.P.C. of the victim was recorded.

After completion of the investigation police Ashok Kumar Soni vs The State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73911121/

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the husband of the victim was working as a Peon in the society, where the petitioner was posted as Branch Manager.
He worked from the year 2009 and he was removed from the services in the year 2019.
He would further submit that a complaint was made by the husband of the victim to the Collector and an enquiry was conducted.
In enquiry, it was found that the husband of the victim remained absent from his service for a considerable time however wages were paid to him.

The earlier complaint was made by the victim on 13.12.2021 making an allegation of sexual assault against the petitioner, wherein it was alleged that since the year 2018 till 2021, she was sexually assaulted by the petitioner.

He would further contend that on 15.12.2021 the victim made an application before the SHO, Outpost Chandaura,
District Surajpur for withdrawal of the complaint made by her on 13.12.2021.

Thereafter, her statement was recorded by the Sub-Inspector on 21.12.2021 where she categorically stated that due to enmity on account of wrong advice, the complaint was made and she has moved the application for withdrawal of the complaint.
The statement of her husband was also recorded on the same day where he stated in the same fashion.
Affidavits were sworn by the victim and her husband in this regard.
Her statement was recorded in the presence of the Executive Magistrate on 22.12.2021 where she categorically stated that she does not want to pursue her complaint dated 13.12.2021.
Mr Mehta would further submit that earlier one WPCR No.223/2022 was filed before the Hon'ble Court to quash the FIR and there was an interim order in his favour.

He would further contend that on account of enmity and ulterior motives, a fresh FIR was lodged on 03.02.2022 making the allegation that in the month of October 2021, she was sexually exploited by the petitioner.
He would also argue that the victim has not given the date of the incident.
He would further argue that the FIR has been lodged with the ulterior motive to wreak vengeance.
He would further submit that no charge can be framed in the absence of date and time according to the provision of Section 211 of the Cr.P.C.

He would also submit that according to the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others, reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335, the FIR, charge sheet and criminal proceedings are liable to be quashed.

entities.text: State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others, reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the victim would oppose.
Ms. Rajni Soren would submit that the victim was sexually assaulted for a period of three years from 2018 to 2021 and thereafter a report was lodged by the victim.
She would further submit that though the date is not given as the victim is illiterate, but she has disclosed the time and place.
She would further contend that the FIR is not an outcome of ulterior motive or vengeance and there is no reason for the victim to lodge a false FIR against the petitioner.

She would also argue that vide Annexure-R/2, R/3 and R/4 the victim has made complaints before the police authorities while she was being compelled to withdraw the FIR registered against the petitioner, which establishes that the petitioner has committed the offence.

She would further argue that one WPCR No.505/2022 was filed for fair investigation and action on her complaint dated 14.01.2022 and the same was disposed of vide order dated 03.07.2023 with liberty to pursue it before the appropriate authorities.
5. Learned counsel for the State would oppose the submission made by learned counsel for the petitioner.

sentences.text: 6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties at length, considered their ri- val submissions made hereinabove and perused the charge sheet.

7. On the perusal of the charge sheet it appears that a written report was lodged by the complainant against the petitioner on 03.02.2022 to the effect that in the month of October 2021 at night about 11-12 P.M., the petitioner forcibly entered the house of the victim and sexually assaulted her and at that time her husband was not present in the house.
It is specifically stated in the FIR that the victim does not remember the date of the incident.
It is also stated that the victim belongs to the Scheduled Tribe community, particularly the Gond caste.

On such complaint, police registered the offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (in short 'the Atrocities Act').

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is also not in dispute that the husband of the victim was working as a Peon in the society, whereas, the petitioner was posted as the Branch Manager.
The husband of the victim was working there on daily wages from 2009 to 2019, thereafter; he remained absent and was removed from the service.
A complaint was made by the husband of the victim to the Collector and an order was passed to conduct an enquiry.
In enquiry, it was found that the husband of the victim was absentee, therefore he was removed from the service and his entire wages had already been paid.
On 13.12.2021 a complaint was made by the victim against the petitioner making an allegation of sexual exploitation.
On 15.12.2021 the victim withdrew her complaint.
Her statement was recorded by the SHO, Sub-Inspector and the Executive Magistrate.
She specifically stated that on account of malice and wrong advice, she lodged the complaint against the petitioner.
The affidavit was given by the victim and her husband.
In the year 2022 again a written complaint was lodged by the victim on 03.02.2022 to the effect that in the month of October 2021, she was sexually exploited by the petitioner.
From a perusal of the FIR, it is clear that the date of the incident was not disclosed.
She was medically examined but no definite opinion was given by the medical officer.

With regard to the Atrocities Act, the offence under Section 3(2)(v) of the Atrocities Act has been registered against the petitioner only on the ground that the victim belongs to the Scheduled Tribe community.

8. Section 212 of the Cr.P.C. says as under:-
"212. Particulars as to time, place and person.
(1) The charge shall contain such particulars as to the time and place of the alleged offence, and the person (if any) against whom, or the thing (if any) in respect of which, it was committed, as are reasonably sufficient to give the accused notice of the matter with which he is charged.
(2) When the accused is charged with criminal breach of trust or dishonest misappropriation of money or other movable property, It shall be sufficient to specify the gross sum or, as the case may be, describe the movable property in respect of which the offence is alleged to have been committed, and the dates between which the offence is alleged to have been committed, without specifying particular items or Ashok Kumar Soni vs The State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73911121/
3 exact dates, and the charge so framed shall be deemed to be a charge of one offence within the meaning of section 219;
Provided that the time included between the first and last of such dates shall not exceed one year."
9.

sentences.text: In the statement recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C., the victim has categorically stated that in the month of October 2021, the petitioner entered her house at night at about 11-12 P.M. and sexually assaulted her and she was threatened for life also, whereas, her relatives and other family members were sleeping in the adjacent rooms and report in this regard was lodged on 03.02.2022.

From a perusal of the entire material, statement of witnesses, and report lodged against the petitioner, it appears that the husband of the victim was removed from service; therefore, the complaint was lodged.

10. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bhajan Lal (supra), in para 102, has held as under:-
"102.

In the backdrop of the interpretation of the various relevant provisions of the Code under Chapter XIV and of the principles of law enunciated by this Court in a series of decisions relating to the exercise of the extraordinary power under Article 226 or the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code which we have extracted and reproduced above, we give the following categories of cases by way of illustration wherein such power could be exercised either to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice, though it may not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulae and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised.

(1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

(2) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.

(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.

(4) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.

(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion Ashok Kumar Soni vs The State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73911121/
4 that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
(6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

entities.text: Ashok Kumar Soni vs The State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."

11. With regard to the Atrocities Act, Section 3(2)(v) is not a substantive offence, if an offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC is not made out then the provision of Section 3(2)(v) of the Atrocities Act would not stand on its own legs.
Taking into consideration the material available on record, I am of the opinion that it is a fit case to quash the FIR, charge sheet and the criminal proceedings.

12. Accordingly, the petition is allowed and the FIR bearing Crime No.25/2022, registered against the petitioner at Police Station Chandaura, District Surajpur, consequential charge sheet and the criminal proceedings of Special Sessions Trial No. 36/2023 pending before the learned Special Judge (Atrocities), Surajpur, District Surajpur (C.G.) are hereby quashed.
